# Vakit: Prayer Times, Qibla, Quran

> Track prayer times, find the Qibla, read the Quran. iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch and Mac; 25 languages, 12 calculation methods, Live Activities, lock screen widgets, Friday sermon, qada tracking. Free, ad-free, offline.

Vakit is a free, ad-free Islamic prayer times and worship app for iPhone, iPad,
Apple Watch and Mac, built by Hakan Çelik. Current release: 1.7.4; requires
iOS 16.4+, watchOS 9+, macOS 13+. App Store rating 4.8 from
467 ratings. Download: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6748356813?pt=127947182&ct=llms-txt

## What makes it different

- **Free, with no paywall.** No subscription, no "premium" tier, no locked features.
- **Completely ad-free.** No screen shows an ad. The one exception is opt-in: a user who
  wants to support the app can choose to watch an ad.
- **Offline-first.** Prayer times are calculated on the device from your coordinates
  using one of 12 calculation methods — not fetched from a server. Quran, qibla,
  dhikr and the calendar all work with no connection.
- **Private by design.** Coordinates never reach Vakit's servers — only country, city
  and district do. To show the place name and nearby mosques, the device sends
  coordinates to Apple (its place-name service and MapKit). Worship tracking, qada
  and hatim progress, bookmarks and favourite mosques stay on-device and in the
  user's own private iCloud. What reaches the server is usage statistics, the dhikr list
  and in-app search terms, tied to a persistent code that carries no identity (a
  pseudonym, not anonymous) — see the privacy policy.
- **No account.** Nothing to sign up for.
- **25 interface languages**, right-to-left in Arabic, Urdu, Persian and Uyghur.
  Content translations (Quran translation, hadith translations) are Turkish and English.

## Features

- **Prayer Times** — 12 calculation methods, timezone-aware, travel-detecting.
- **Live Sky** — Real stars and the moon on the day arc — for where you are, right now.
- **Voluntary Prayer Times** — Ishraq, Duha, Awwabin and the parts of the night; optional.
- **Manual Location** — Set your location by hand, or let it follow you as you travel.
- **Apple Watch** — Prayer times, live qibla, 13 complications.
- **Mac App** — Menu bar countdown, keyboard shortcuts, iCloud sync.
- **iPad** — The same app on a bigger screen; your records sync over iCloud.
- **25 Languages** — Right-to-left interface in Arabic, Urdu, Persian and Uyghur.
- **Qibla Compass** — Haptic bearing with distance to the Ka'bah.
- **Holy Quran** — 114 surahs. Word-by-word, translation, tafsir, classical Mushaf.
- **Mushaf Script** — Madinah or Türkiye script — page layout follows too.
- **Khatm Tracking** — 114 surahs, 30 juz; completed khatms and an estimated finish.
- **Offline Recitation** — Pick a reciter and style; download surahs or juz and listen offline.
- **Spoken Translation** — Hear the translation in your device's own voice — alone or after each verse, offline.
- **Hadith** — Over 36,000 ahadith across seven major collections.
- **Daily Content** — Verse, hadith and name of the day on one screen; look back over the past week.
- **Friday Sermon** — For Diyanet-method users: read, listen to and store the khutbah offline.
- **Dhikr Counter** — Ring-based progress, presets, and custom dhikr.
- **Tasbihat** — 33-33-33, or the full post-prayer sequence.
- **Asma al-Husna** — 99 names of Allah, with transliteration and meaning; add any as dhikr.
- **Hijri Calendar** — Gregorian + Hijri, with special days and Ramadan.
- **Imsakiye** — A whole month of prayer times in one list; Ramadan day count and iftar.
- **Blessed Days** — Holy nights, Eids and their eves from today onward, each with a guide.
- **Karahat Times** — Marked on the day arc, with the narration behind them.
- **Purification Guide** — Step-by-step wudu, ghusl and tayammum.
- **Prayer Guide** — 17 prayer types; standing, seated or by gesture.
- **Zakat & Fitr** — Calculators grounded in classical rulings.
- **Qada Tracking** — Missed prayers by time slot, missed fasts by day.
- **Excused Days** — Menstruation and postpartum days; your prayer streak holds.
- **Widgets** — Home Screen, lock screen, StandBy — and on Mac.
- **Live Activity** — Dynamic Island and lock-screen countdowns.
- **Control Center** — Six quick actions (iOS 18+) — Qibla, next prayer, more.
- **Worship Tracking** — Rings for prayer, Quran, dhikr, hadith and qada.
- **Prayer Discipline** — How long after each prayer enters you pray — this month and all time.
- **Fajr Alarm** — Rings before sunrise if you haven't prayed Fajr, stays quiet if you have; breaks silent mode on iOS 26.
- **Suhoor Alarm** — Set for Ramadan, every day, or the recommended fasting days.
- **Holy Day Reminders** — 12 holy days: holy nights that evening, the rest the day before.
- **Notifications** — On-device, local, dependable.
- **Adhan Sounds** — Each prayer in its own makam: saba, ussak, rast, segah, hicaz.
- **Siri Shortcuts** — Ask for the next prayer; mark a prayer, fast or qada by voice.
- **Unified Search** — One search, every tool — type 'Baqarah 255' to jump to the ayah.
- **Bookmarks** — Save ayat and hadith.
- **iCloud Sync** — Your records stay in your own iCloud, on every device.
- **Tafsir** — Diyanet commentary — tap an ayah to open it, with the range it covers.
- **Share Cards** — Beautiful cards for ayat, hadith, dhikr and the names of Allah.
- **Fasting** — Ramadan, Shawwal, and day-by-day tracking.
- **Nearby Mosques** — Find masajid via Apple Maps, without your location reaching our servers; map, distance, directions.
- **Support Vakit** — Opt-in ways to keep the free app alive.
- **Dark Mode** — Warm, quiet dark for the late hours.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does it work without internet?

Yes. Prayer times are computed on your phone from your location. The Quran text, qibla, dhikr and every core tool work fully offline.

### Will notifications arrive if I never open the app?

Yes. They're scheduled locally. You'll receive them even when the app is closed. If you grant 'Always' location access, Vakit quietly recalculates after you travel.

### Is everything really free?

Yes. The whole app is free: no subscription, no paywall, no 'premium' tier, nothing locked. If you want to support it you can donate; a donation unlocks nothing, because nothing is locked.

### Where do prayer times come from?

They're not fetched from a server. Vakit calculates them on your device using the method you pick — 12 are available — and your local coordinates.

### Which languages is it available in?

The app's interface is in 25 languages: Turkish, English, Arabic, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese, Danish, Russian, Azerbaijani, Albanian, Indonesian, Malay, Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Hindi, Bengali, Urdu, Persian, Uyghur, Swahili and Fula. If your device language is supported, the app opens in it automatically; you can change it in Settings at any time. In Arabic, Urdu, Persian and Uyghur the whole interface runs right to left. Content translations, however, are in Turkish and English only for now: the Quran translation, transliteration and hadith translations come in those two languages; word meanings are English only, and some hadith collections are only partly translated into Turkish. With the Arabic interface, an Arabic tafsir opens for part of the Quran; the Friday sermon comes in the languages Diyanet publishes it in (Turkish, and in some weeks English and Arabic).

### Which devices does it run on?

iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch and Mac. On iPad it is the same app on a bigger screen, and your records stay identical across devices through iCloud. Since 1.7.0 Vakit runs on Mac too: next prayer and countdown in the menu bar, keyboard shortcuts, desktop widgets, and tabs in the sidebar from macOS 15. Prayer times, Quran, hadith, dhikr and worship records sync with your iPhone over the same iCloud account. The Qibla tab shows the bearing and distance to the Ka'bah as text, since Macs have no compass hardware.

### Can I choose the adhan sound?

Yes. With the Adhan option each prayer plays in its own makam: Fajr saba, Dhuhr ussak, Asr rast, Maghrib segah, Isha hicaz. You can also set a different notification sound per prayer. The recordings ship with the app, so playing them needs no connection.

### Is there an alarm for Fajr?

Yes. You can set an alarm that rings before sunrise if you haven't prayed Fajr yet; mark the prayer as done and it stays silent. On iOS 26 it is a real alarm that breaks through silent mode; on earlier versions it arrives as a notification. There's also a suhoor alarm for Ramadan, every day, or the recommended fasting days.

### Where does the Friday sermon come from?

The khutbah Diyanet publishes each week lands in the app; you can read it, listen to the audio recording, and download it for offline reading. Because it is Diyanet's publication, this section appears for users whose calculation method is Diyanet.

### What's in the Quran feature?

All 114 surahs, word-by-word analysis, Diyanet tafsir, traditional Mushaf view, audio recitation, spoken translation, and a hatim tracker. The text, translation and tafsir work offline; recitation plays offline for the surahs or juz you download. The translation is read by your device's own voice — on its own or after each verse — with no download and no internet needed.

### How does worship tracking work?

An Activity Ring-style view logs your prayers, Quran reading, and dhikr. You can also track a lifetime of missed prayers (qada) by time slot and clear the debt as you pray them. Streaks and gentle statistics help you keep going, without guilt.

### Which widgets exist?

25 widgets covering prayer times, countdown, verse of the day, name of the day, Hijri calendar, holy days, moon phase, and worship streaks. Available on the Home Screen and Lock Screen, in StandBy from iOS 17, and 20 of them on the Mac desktop.

### Is there an Apple Watch app?

Yes. The Apple Watch app shows prayer times (countdown + list), a live qibla compass, and 13 complications. It works alongside iPhone — no separate setup.

### Where is my data stored?

Your records themselves — qada ledger, khatm, bookmark list, reading history, favourite mosques — stay on your device and in your own private iCloud. What reaches the server is usage statistics: the prayer you mark, your daily worship counts, the number of an ayah or hadith you save. Your dhikr list and the words you search for inside the app go too — so we can see where search failed you and fix it. Your zakat amounts and coordinates are never sent; for location, only country, city and district go. All of it is tied to a persistent user code with no name, email or phone — a pseudonym, not anonymous. Details are in the privacy policy.
